statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the only discoverable archetype. The requested root and /sitemap.xml return 404; robots.txt exposes no route hints and the page has no links, so no additional representative route could be discovered.

paths.description: Requested root URL and its server-rendered 404/error archetype. This is the only discoverable page: the DOM has no links, robots.txt lists no routes, and /sitemap.xml returns 404. Authenticated or unlinked routes were not covered because none could be discovered safely.

findings.summary: The error page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is pixel-equivalent to the light capture; CSS probe reports no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark schemes at document/root level and use adaptive surface/text tokens, following dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: The 404 state provides no guided route back to useful content.
findings.evidence: DOM and screenshots show no link, navigation landmark, home action, search action, or focus destination.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prominent, descriptive link to the service home page and, if available, search or support routes; use semantic navigation and clear attention hierarchy.

findings.summary: The page identifies a 404 but exposes no primary next action.
findings.evidence: First-viewport screenshot shows only “404 Not Found”; evaluate reports interactive=0 and headings=0.
findings.suggestedFix: Explain what happened in user language and make “Return to home” the clear primary action.

findings.summary: The requested public root URL is a dead end rather than a completable primary journey.
findings.evidence: The main document returns HTTP 404 and the rendered DOM has zero links, forms, buttons, or other continuation paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore or redirect the public root to the intended service entry point; keep a recovery-oriented 404 template for genuinely unknown paths.

findings.summary: The error state has no retry, back, home, search, or support recovery.
findings.evidence: The 404 screenshot and DOM show only status text and no actionable recovery control.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide explicit recovery actions and preserve enough context to help users continue.

findings.summary: A render-blocking third-party font delays a 13-character error page.
findings.evidence: HAR identifies the parser-inserted Google Fonts stylesheet as VeryHigh/render-blocking; stylesheet took 615 ms, font 372 ms, and trace LCP reached 2382 ms despite the tiny page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a system font on the error template or self-host/subset the font with non-blocking loading and a stable fallback; avoid prioritising non-critical font work.

findings.summary: The document has no main landmark or heading structure.
findings.evidence: Axe reports landmark-one-main, page-has-heading-one, and region violations; DOM probe reports landmarks=[] and headings=[].
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the error content in <main> and use an <h1> for the user-facing error heading, preserving the concise visual treatment.

findings.summary: Metadata is generic and has no description.
findings.evidence: Rendered title is only “Not Found” and meta[name=description] is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a service-specific error title and concise description that identifies the site and recovery purpose.

findings.summary: The error page is mobile-friendly but has no crawlable recovery link.
findings.evidence: Viewport metadata and mobile reflow pass, robots allows crawling, but the DOM contains zero anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add real href-based links with descriptive text to home and other useful public destinations.

findings.summary: The public root returns 404 and the host exposes no sitemap at /sitemap.xml.
findings.evidence: HAR/discoverability record fetchedStatus=404 for the root; /sitemap.xml also returns the generic 404 response; no canonical URL is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the intended root with HTTP 200 (or a deliberate permanent redirect), publish a consistent sitemap for public routes, and add canonical signals where appropriate.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline transport/content hardening headers are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive finds no Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, or X-Content-Type-Options; all are reported missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS after confirming HTTPS coverage, a restrictive CSP appropriate to the template, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced framing, referrer, and permission defenses are not configured.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive finds neither frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options nor Referrer-Policy nor Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors in CSP (or X-Frame-Options where needed), a conservative Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The network/HTTP failure state is visible but not recoverable.
findings.evidence: The observed 404 response renders a bare message with no retry, home, search, support, or diagnostic context.
findings.suggestedFix: Build a resilient error template with useful recovery actions and ensure unknown routes return it while the intended root remains available.
